title: Handle offline/mobile burst re-uploads and duplicate token credits in metering pipeline
creator: Amira Park
description:
Problem summary: Mobile/offline clients buffer streaming responses and later re-upload them after reconnect. The uploads occasionally contain overlapping fragments or truncated suffixes and may be retried with different client-generated request ids. This results in duplicate token credits and occasional under/over-counting against customer quotas. We see this as periodic spikes in metering ingestion and erroneous billing adjustments.

Observed symptoms: repeated token tallies for the same logical response, mid-session replays that create overlapping token ranges, and clients that append residual partial fragments on top of previously uploaded payloads. Existing dedupe heuristics (frame id + session id) fail because clients generate new request ids after reconnect or when signing keys rotate.

Why this matters: duplicates directly impact customer billing accuracy and quota enforcement, undermining trust for mobile-first customers and leading to support escalations. This ticket scopes detection, dedupe, reconciliation, and retro-crediting for offline/mobile reuploads with minimal latency impact on the ingestion pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion pipeline dedupes >= 99.9% of duplicate token events from offline/mobile re-uploads in our synthetic replay tests
No customer sees >1% unexplained billing drift attributable to mobile reuploads in the first 30d after rollout
System produces a clear per-session watermark and reconciliation logs for any retro-credit operations
Feature toggled behind a runtime flag and can be rolled back within 1 hour
End-to-end tests added to CI that simulate reconnect+reupload, partial overlap, and truncated-suffix cases
proposed_solution: Require clients to attach a stable session fingerprint when possible (client_session_fingerprint). For older clients, accept best-effort but fallback to server heuristics.

Introduce idempotency window: group fragments by (customer_id, model, session_fingerprint, stream_start_timestamp) and compute ordered checksums (rolling-hash) for dedupe instead of relying purely on request_id
Detect overlapping uploads by computing a lightweight token-range signature (first N tokens hash, last N tokens hash, total token count) and use those signatures to decide duplicate crediting
Add reconciler job that runs periodically to find near-duplicate consumption entries within a sliding 24-hour window and issue retroactive credits via the billing ledger with audit records
Expose a new 'metering.replay' counter and dashboard to surface reupload activity and the reconciler's actions
Safety: conservative approach - do not auto-delete logged events; reconciler creates compensating ledger entries to preserve auditability
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy dedupe logic to ingestion in region us-west-2 behind feature flag, run for 48h on 5% of mobile traffic
Phase 2 (observe): Increase to 25% for 7 days. Monitor false-positive dedupe rate and billing drift metrics
Phase 3 (global): 100% mobile traffic after SLOs validated. Turn on reconciler in read-only mode to surface candidates for manual review for 3 days
Phase 4 (auto-correct): Enable automatic retro-crediting with throttling limits and alerting; keep rollback toggle available
Rollback: feature flag off and reconciler paused; compensating entries are reversible via standard ledger tooling
test_plan: Unit tests for checksum generation and token-range signature logic
E2E CI test that spins up a local ingestion harness and replays scripted reconnect scenarios with variable client ids
Chaos test: simulate mobile network flaps and double-POSTs to verify idempotency window
Long-run synthetic test: replay 1M mobile events with 0-10% duplicate uploads and assert dedupe rate and processing latency targets
Billing regression test: integrate with billing-staging to ensure reconciler creates compensating ledger entries with correct amounts
metrics_and_alerts: alert: HighDuplicateRate (firing if duplicate rate > 0.5% for 10m)
implementation_notes: Prefer streaming-safe checksums (rolling polynomial hash) to avoid O(L) expensive comparisons for long transcripts
Keep dedupe index TTL equal to maximum expected reconnect window (configurable; default 48h)
Reconciler should run in a low-priority batch pool and rate-limit writes to the billing ledger to avoid thundering credit storms
If session_fingerprint is missing, fall back to (ip_sign, user_agent_hash, approximate_start_ts) with lower confidence score
Add telemetry tag 'dedupe_confidence' to walked events so downstream billing pipelines can surface uncertain decisions to ops
notes: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after multiple support cases and an incident postmortem (INC-2026-02-MOB-METER) showing spike in duplicate credits.
2026-03-04: Spike analysis - duplicates concentrated in older Android SDK versions behind corporate proxies.
2026-03-06: Eng sync: agreed to implement signature-based dedupe + reconciler rather than client-only migration (tradeoff: server complexity vs. customer migration friction).
2026-03-09: Proto PR (link above) shows dedupe reduces duplicate counts by ~92% on sampled traffic; edge cases remain for truncated-suffix uploads.
2026-03-12: Diego started integration with ledger team; flagged need for billing ops runbook for manual reconciliations during canary.
